547	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
548	
549	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
550	
551	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
552	
553	### How connector nodes reference bindings
554	
555	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
556	
557	```json
558	"context": [
559	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
560	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
561	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
562	]
563	```
564	
565	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
566	
567	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
568	
569	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)
570	
571	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. The schema below is the shape the CLI emits, for **inspection** when debugging a flow's binding state and as the planned shape for the **No-Live-Tenant** flow's sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` (see § No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration above). Per the [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) rules, `bindings[]` is part of the CLI-owned envelope for connector / connector-trigger / managed HTTP nodes.
572	
573	For every unique connection used in the flow, `node configure` appends **two entries** to top-level `bindings[]`:
574	
575	```json
576	"bindings": [
577	  {
578	    "id": "<CONN_BINDING_ID>",
579	    "name": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
580	    "type": "string",
581	    "resource": "Connection",
582	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
583	    "default": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
584	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
585	  },
586	  {
587	    "id": "<FOLDER_BINDING_ID>",
588	    "name": "FolderKey",
589	    "type": "string",
590	    "resource": "Connection",
591	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
592	    "default": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
593	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
594	  }
595	]
596	```
597	
598	| Field | Value |
599	|-------|-------|
600	| `id` | Unique string within the file. Descriptive (e.g. `bJiraConn`) or short random (e.g. `bKEFLMRB2`). |
601	| `name` (connection binding) | The IS connection name (e.g. `"chandu.lella@uipath.com #3"`). `uip maestro flow node configure` fetches this from IS automatically — this is the supported path. The placeholder form `"<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"` appears in the table for reference only (e.g. when inspecting a flow whose bindings have not yet been configured); it must match the definition's `model.context[].connection` placeholder (without the `<bindings.` prefix and `>` suffix). |
602	| `name` (folder binding) | Literal `"FolderKey"` — matches `<bindings.FolderKey>`. |
603	| `type` | Always `"string"`. |
604	| `resource` | Always `"Connection"` — capital C, case-sensitive. |
605	| `resourceKey` | The connection UUID from `uip is connections list`. **Same UUID on both bindings.** |
606	| `default` | Connection binding → connection UUID. Folder binding → folder key. |
607	| `propertyAttribute` | `"ConnectionId"` or `"FolderKey"` — case matters. |
608	
609	The connector node instance carries no `model` block and no binding/context data. `uip maestro flow node configure` populates only `inputs.detail` on the instance and writes the two top-level `bindings[]` entries — claiming the empty `ConnectionId` stub that `node add` hoisted (matched by name) and adding the `FolderKey` row. The connection UUID is held on the binding entry (`resourceKey`), not on the node.
610	
611	> **An empty-keyed Connection binding is a defect, not a cosmetic nit.** A `bindings[]` row with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"`, and `resourceKey: ""` faults Studio Web at runtime with `Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'Connection')`. `node add` hoists exactly one such stub (`name: "<connector-key> connection"`); `node configure` **claims it in place** (matching by that name), so a fully configured connector leaves no empty row — do not expect a "duplicate" empty pair, and never hand-edit `bindings[]` to remove one (it is CLI-owned). The only legitimate empty stub is the No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration case above, where the node is deliberately left unconfigured and the flow is known not to pass `flow validate` yet. An empty stub that survives a real `node configure` — or lingers after a connector node is removed — is a CLI bug to report, not something to paper over by hand.
612	
613	**Share bindings across nodes using the same connection.** If two connector nodes share the same `<CONNECTION_UUID>`, reuse the same two binding entries — do not add duplicates. Matching is by `name` only (the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder is unique per connector), so any node whose definition resolves against `<bindings.<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection>` picks up the shared binding pair.

733	### Debug Tips
734	
735	1. **Always check top-level `bindings[]` in the `.flow` file** — connector nodes silently fail if a binding is missing or malformed. Compare against the CLI-emitted `bindings[]` shape documented above (§ Top-level `bindings[]` shape). Do not inspect `bindings_v2.json` as ground truth; it is regenerated from the `.flow` on every debug/pack.
736	2. **Compare inputs against metadataFile** — the full metadata (from `is resources describe`) has every field with types, descriptions, and whether it's required
737	3. **`flow validate` does NOT catch connector-specific issues** — validation only checks JSON schema and graph structure. Missing `inputs.detail` fields, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime (`flow debug`)
738	4. **If a connector key doesn't work** — list all connectors: `uip is connectors list --output json`. Keys are often prefixed with `uipath-`
739	5. **Query/path parameters** — some required parameters appear only in the metadataFile `parameters` section, not in `requestFields`. Check both.
740	6. **`node configure` populates bindings automatically** — it appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries and populates `inputs.detail`. The generated `bindings_v2.json` follows from these at debug/pack time. If you cannot run `node configure` (no live tenant, sandbox forbids it, planning-only request), record the planned binding entries in the sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` per the No-Live-Tenant flow above — do not author `bindings[]` directly on the `.flow` as a substitute, and note that the flow will not pass `flow validate` until a real `node configure` runs.

1	# Loop Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.loop`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.loop --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input ports `input` and `loopBack`, output ports `success` and `output`, required input `collection`. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	### Loop node
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "id": "loop1",
22	  "type": "core.logic.loop",
23	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
24	  "display": { "label": "Loop over items" },
25	  "inputs": {
26	    "collection": "=js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items",
27	    "parallel": false
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	> **Collection source shape depends on the node type.** Connector `list` activities return the bare array — `"collection": "=js:$vars.searchIssuesByJql1.output"`, NOT `.output.issues` / `.output.items`. HTTP nodes differ — envelope preserved: `.output.body.<key>` as above. See [connector/impl.md — Connector output shape](../connector/impl.md).
33	
34	Set `"parallel": true` to execute all iterations concurrently.
35	
36	### Loop body nodes — `parentId` required
37	
38	Every node inside the loop body **must** have `"parentId"` set to the loop node's ID. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is part of the loop and variableUpdates will not fire per-iteration.
39	
40	```json
41	{
42	  "id": "processItem",
43	  "type": "core.action.script",
44	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
45	  "display": { "label": "Process item" },
46	  "inputs": {
47	    "script": "return $vars.product * $vars.loop1.currentItem"
48	  },
49	  "parentId": "loop1"
50	}
51	```
52	
53	> **Critical:** If you omit `parentId`, the node executes outside the loop context. State variables will not update across iterations and loop outputs like `currentItem` will be inaccessible.
54	
55	## Adding / Editing
56	
57	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs` and `parentId`.
58	
59	### CLI carve-out nodes inside a loop
60	
61	When adding a CLI carve-out node (connector, connector trigger, or managed HTTP) inside a loop, pass `--parent` to set `parentId` automatically:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <FLOW_PATH> core.action.http.v2 --label "Fetch data" --parent <LOOP_ID> --output json
65	uip maestro flow node add <FLOW_PATH> <CONNECTOR_NODE_TYPE> --label "Get record" --parent <LOOP_ID> --output json
66	```
67	
68	`--parent` validates the parent node exists and sets `parentId` on the new node. For non-carve-out node types (script, end, etc.), set `"parentId"` directly in the JSON — see the examples above.
69	
70	## Wiring
71	
72	Loop nodes have a specific wiring pattern:
73	
74	- `input` — entry from upstream
75	- `output` — into the loop body (first body node)
76	- `loopBack` — return from last body node back to loop
77	- `success` — exit after loop completes (to next downstream node)
78	
79	See [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md) for edge add procedures.
80	
81	## Accessing Loop Variables Inside Body
82	
83	Inside the loop body, access the current item via `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`:
84	
85	```javascript
86	// In a Script node inside the loop body (parentId must be set to the loop node)
87	const item = $vars.loop1.currentItem;
88	const index = $vars.loop1.currentIndex;
89	return { processed: item.name.toUpperCase(), position: index };
90	```
91	
92	| Variable | Description |
93	| --- | --- |
94	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | The item being processed in this iteration |
95	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` | 0-based iteration index |
96	| `$vars.<loopId>.collection` | The full collection being iterated |
97	
98	> **Do not use `iterator.currentItem`.** The correct access pattern is `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
99	
100	### Required node variables for loop outputs
101	
102	For `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` etc. to resolve, you must add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`:
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "variables": {
107	    "nodes": [
108	      {
109	        "id": "loop1.currentItem",
110	        "type": "any",
111	        "description": "The current item being iterated in the loop",
112	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" }
113	      },
114	      {
115	        "id": "loop1.currentIndex",
116	        "type": "number",
117	        "description": "The current iteration index (0-based)",
118	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" }
119	      },
120	      {
121	        "id": "loop1.collection",
122	        "type": "array",
123	        "description": "The collection being iterated over",
124	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" }
125	      },
126	      {
127	        "id": "loop1.output",
128	        "type": "array",
129	        "description": "Aggregated results from all loop iterations",
130	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" }
131	      }
132	    ]
133	  }
134	}
135	```

137	## State Accumulation with variableUpdates
138	
139	To accumulate state across loop iterations (counters, running totals), use an `inout` variable with a `variableUpdate` on the body node:
140	
141	```json
142	{
143	  "variables": {
144	    "globals": [
145	      {
146	        "id": "runningTotal",
147	        "direction": "inout",
148	        "type": "number",
149	        "defaultValue": 0
150	      }
151	    ],
152	    "variableUpdates": {
153	      "bodyNode": [
154	        {
155	          "variableId": "runningTotal",
156	          "expression": "=js:$vars.bodyNode.output"
157	        }
158	      ]
159	    }
160	  }
161	}
162	```
163	
164	The variableUpdate fires after each iteration, so the `inout` variable carries the accumulated value into the next iteration.
165	
166	> **Critical:** The variableUpdate expression **cannot** access loop iteration variables like `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`. These are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). If you need to compute using `currentItem`, do the computation in the script and reference the script's output in the variableUpdate.
167	
168	## Complete Example — Loop with State Accumulation
169	
170	A flow that iterates over a collection, accumulates a result in an `inout` variable via a Script body node, and outputs the final value.
171	
172	```json
173	{
174	  "nodes": [
175	    {
176	      "id": "start",
177	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
178	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
179	      "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
180	      "inputs": { "entryPointId": "..." }
181	    },
182	    {
183	      "id": "loop1",
184	      "type": "core.logic.loop",
185	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
186	      "display": { "label": "Loop" },
187	      "inputs": { "collection": "=js:$vars.inputItems", "parallel": false }
188	    },
189	    {
190	      "id": "bodyScript",
191	      "type": "core.action.script",
192	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
193	      "display": { "label": "Process item" },
194	      "inputs": {
195	        "script": "return $vars.accumulator + $vars.loop1.currentItem;"
196	      },
197	      "parentId": "loop1"
198	    },
199	    {
200	      "id": "end1",
201	      "type": "core.control.end",
202	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
203	      "display": { "label": "End" },
204	      "inputs": {},
205	      "outputs": {
206	        "result": { "source": "=js:$vars.accumulator" }
207	      }
208	    }
209	  ],
210	  "edges": [
211	    { "id": "e1", "sourceNodeId": "start", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "input" },
212	    { "id": "e2", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "bodyScript", "targetPort": "input" },
213	    { "id": "e3", "sourceNodeId": "bodyScript", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "loopBack" },
214	    { "id": "e4", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "end1", "targetPort": "input" }
215	  ],
216	  "variables": {
217	    "globals": [
218	      { "id": "inputItems", "direction": "in", "type": "array", "defaultValue": [] },
219	      { "id": "accumulator", "direction": "inout", "type": "number", "defaultValue": 0 },
220	      { "id": "result", "direction": "out", "type": "number" }
221	    ],
222	    "nodes": [
223	      { "id": "loop1.currentItem", "type": "any", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" } },
224	      { "id": "loop1.currentIndex", "type": "number", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" } },
225	      { "id": "loop1.collection", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" } },
226	      { "id": "loop1.output", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" } },
227	      { "id": "bodyScript.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "bodyScript", "outputId": "output" } },
228	      { "id": "bodyScript.error", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "bodyScript", "outputId": "error" } }
229	    ],
230	    "variableUpdates": {
231	      "bodyScript": [
232	        { "variableId": "accumulator", "expression": "=js:$vars.bodyScript.output" }
233	      ]
234	    }
235	  }
236	}
237	```
238	
239	Key points in this pattern:
240	- `bodyScript` has `"parentId": "loop1"` — places it inside the loop
241	- Script accesses `$vars.loop1.currentItem` for the current iteration value
242	- `variableUpdate` on `bodyScript` writes the script's return value back to `accumulator`
243	- `accumulator` is `inout` so it persists across iterations
244	- End node maps the final accumulated value to the `out` variable
